record.paper_title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
record.original_question: How should next-to-leading-twist effects be incorporated in Drell-Yan-like processes once perturbative NNLO calculations and data reach a precision where those effects can no longer be safely ignored, especially given that infrared divergences in higher-twist contributions do not cancel beyond the one-loop level for these processes?

evidence.quote: What is worse, for these processes the infrared divergencies in higher-twist contributions do not cancel beyond the one-loop level.68, 70, 80–82
The perturbative NNLO calculations, as well as the data are reaching a precision at which it will no longer be safe to ignore Next to Leading Twist effects.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Drell-Yan-like inclusive hard-scattering processes (e.g., $h_1 h_2 \to \gamma^*/Z/W + X$ with the lepton-pair invariant mass $Q$ large). The standard collinear factorization formula expresses the cross section as a convolution of perturbative partonic coefficient functions with leading-twist (twist-2) parton distribution functions, modulo power-suppressed corrections of order $(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}/Q)^n$ associated with higher-twist matrix elements.

It is known that for these Drell-Yan-like processes the infrared (collinear/soft) divergences appearing in the higher-twist (in particular, next-to-leading-twist, twist-3 and twist-4) contributions to the partonic cross sections do not cancel beyond the one-loop level against the corresponding ultraviolet renormalization of higher-twist operator matrix elements; equivalently, no all-order collinear factorization theorem for next-to-leading-twist contributions is currently established for Drell-Yan.

Problem. Formulate a consistent and predictive framework for incorporating next-to-leading-twist (power-suppressed, $\mathcal{O}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}^2/Q^2)$) contributions into the theoretical description of Drell-Yan-like processes that:

(a) provides a well-defined operator basis of higher-twist distributions and their evolution equations;
(b) yields finite, infrared-safe partonic coefficient functions at two-loop order and beyond, by either proving cancellation of the residual infrared divergences against suitable redefinitions of higher-twist matrix elements, or by establishing a generalized factorization theorem in which such divergences are systematically absorbed; and
(c) is compatible with the precision of NNLO (and higher) perturbative calculations for the leading-twist part, so that combined leading-plus-next-to-leading-twist predictions can be confronted with high-precision Drell-Yan data.

Either prove such a factorization/subtraction scheme exists at all orders (or to a specified order) for Drell-Yan-like processes, or demonstrate an obstruction to its existence.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches reveal substantial progress on leading-twist NNLO infrared subtraction for Drell-Yan (N-jettiness, nested subtractions, local counterterms), but no established all-order factorization theorem for next-to-leading-twist contributions in Drell-Yan-like processes. The non-cancellation of infrared divergences in higher-twist contributions beyond one-loop remains a recognized open issue, with no published resolution found.

status_evidence.title: Removing infrared divergences from two-loop integrals
status_evidence.snippet: Systematic method for removal of infrared singularities by adding counterterms that approximate and cancel divergent limits point-by-point at the integrand level.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses IR cancellation at two-loop for leading-twist Drell-Yan, but does not extend to higher-twist factorization.

status_evidence.title: Towards the two-loop electroweak corrections to the Drell-Yan process: the infrared structure
status_evidence.snippet: Two-loop infrared structure of Drell-Yan studied within standard collinear factorization at leading twist.
status_evidence.claim: Current state-of-the-art two-loop Drell-Yan calculations remain at leading twist; higher-twist IR issues are not addressed.
